d1: The binding is malformed (the “(...)” fragment) and does not clearly identify which mug or which headphones to compare. More importantly, the edited image shows multiple mug-like objects and headphones, including a mug left of the headphones and another to their right; the traces appear to select only the right-hand mug and therefore pass a narrow positional check. Clarify the binding to evaluate the requested mug’s movement relative to the source image, and make the decision criterion account for whether the requested change progressed and is complete across the relevant objects, rather than treating any mug on the right as sufficient. The reference “partial” constrains the aggregate, but is not atomic ground truth: inspect the source/edited correspondence and preserve uncertainty if identity or progress cannot be established. The five repeated high-confidence “yes” traces indicate a systematic binding/criterion issue, not independent confirmation. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the edited image show the original blue mug moved to the right of the headphones, rather than merely showing any mug on the right?
findings.criteria: Compare source and edited images to identify the blue mug and determine whether that same mug is now to the right of the headphones. A different mug appearing on the right does not establish the requested move.
findings.evidence: The source shows one blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image shows a blue, blurred-looking shape left of the headphones, a small light-colored mug near the headphones, and another mug on the far right. The saved d1 observations report only that a visible mug is to the right; they do not establish which mug corresponds to the source mug.
findings.rationale: The broad relative-position check passes, but the instruction asks to move the source mug. The edited image raises an identity/continuity question that the existing check and observations do not resolve, so the pass alone may overclaim fulfillment.

transactions.reason: The repeated passes identify only a mug on the right, not the source mug. The source contains a blue mug left of the black headphones; the edited image contains a blurred blue shape on the left and two light-colored mugs, including one on the right. Revise the binding to establish source-to-edit correspondence rather than accepting any right-hand mug, retaining uncertainty when correspondence cannot be established.

decisions.question: Has the mug identified in the source image been moved to the right of the corresponding headphones in the edited image?
decisions.criteria: Pass if comparison of the source and edited images establishes that the source mug has been relocated and is visibly to the right of the corresponding headphones. A different or additional mug on the right does not establish satisfaction. Fail if the source mug is identifiable in the edited image and has not been moved to the right of the headphones. Return unknown if the mug's identity, relocation, or relative position cannot be established reliably; do not infer failure solely from ambiguous correspondence.
decisions.binding: Track the blue handled mug initially left of the black over-ear headphones in the SOURCE image to its corresponding object in the EDITED image, using visible appearance, shape, handle, and scene correspondence. Compare that mug with the edited counterpart of the source headphones. Consider all candidate mugs and the blurred blue shape at the original location; do not select the far-right mug merely because its position fits the request.
